preamble: In many varieties of English the aspirated /t/ of onset /tr/ clusters (tree, street) is affricated through coarticulation with the following postalveolar or retroflex approximant, so that tree comes to resemble 'chree'. The result is most often transcribed as a postalveolar [tʃ], but its quality varies with the speaker's /r/, and descriptions also give a retroflex-like [tʂ] or [tʂɻ] for speakers with retroflex /r/. Magloughlin's study of Raleigh, North Carolina treats it as a sound change in progress that is becoming phonologized. The retroflex realization is a speaker-dependent subtype of the better-attested tʰ > tʃ pattern; no other language has a verified case of tʰ > ʈʂ.

examples.note: Onset /tr/ affricates and is variously realized as [tʃɹ], [tʂ] or [tʂɻ], depending on the articulation of /r/. Heterosyllabic /t.r/ (rat-race) does not affricate.

sources: Magloughlin, L. (2018). /tɹ/ and /dɹ/ in North American English: Phonologization of a Coarticulatory Effect. PhD dissertation, University of Ottawa. https://doi.org/10.20381/ruor-21856
